description: Database schema extension: add ngo_registrations table and ngo_registration_id column to users table. This is the foundation for all other features and must be done first.
steps: 1. Modify db.py SCHEMA string to add ngo_registrations table with: id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ngo_id TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL (format NGO-1001), org_name TEXT NOT NULL, official_reg_number TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, registration_type TEXT NOT NULL (Trust/Society/Section 8 Company/Foundation/Other), email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, contact_number TEXT NOT NULL, address TEXT NOT NULL, password_hash TEXT NOT NULL, certificate_filename TEXT, email_verified INTEGER DEFAULT 0, verification_token TEXT, status TEXT DEFAULT 'PENDING' CHECK (status IN ('PENDING','APPROVED','REJECTED')), rejection_reason TEXT, applied_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, reviewed_at TEXT, reviewed_by INTEGER REFERENCES users(id).

2. Add migration-safe ALTER TABLE users to add ngo_registration_id INTEGER column. Use a guard pattern: wrap in try/except or check column existence first to handle existing databases. Pattern: db().execute('ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN ngo_registration_id INTEGER'); catch sqlite3.OperationalError if column exists.

3. Test schema by deleting reliefgrid.db and running python app.py. Verify ngo_registrations table exists with: sqlite3 reliefgrid.db '.schema ngo_registrations'. Verify users table has new column with: sqlite3 reliefgrid.db '.schema users'.
4. Test backward compatibility: with fresh db, login as existing seed users (admin@reliefgrid.org/admin123, riverside@ngo.org/relief123) should work normally with ngo_registration_id=NULL.
acceptance_criteria: ngo_registrations table exists with all specified columns and constraints
users table has ngo_registration_id column without breaking existing data
Existing seed users login successfully after schema change
Schema migration is safe to run on existing databases (idempotent)
verification: Run python app.py and verify startup succeeds without errors
Run sqlite3 reliefgrid.db '.schema ngo_registrations' - table exists with all columns
Run sqlite3 reliefgrid.db '.schema users' - ngo_registration_id column present
Visit http://127.0.0.1:5000/login and login as admin@reliefgrid.org/admin123 - succeeds
Visit http://127.0.0.1:5000/login and login as riverside@ngo.org/relief123 - succeeds
findings:

- users table successfully extended with ngo_registration_id INTEGER column
